title: Lior and the Well
premise: Dominic Thornbury, an urban explorer who trusts only what he can document, begins mapping tunnels beneath his late grandmother's village that appear on no survey. Every photograph he took in her house now shows an extra chair at the kitchen table, and the villagers hum a harvest song whose final verse no one will teach him. As the harvest moon rises, Dominic learns the chair belongs to him—that he was promised to the well before he was born—and that the song's last verse is a refusal. By singing everything except the final verse, he breaks the bargain, claims a found family among the villagers who once abandoned him to it, and chooses an identity written by memory rather than debt.
about_author: Oscar Villalobos is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent a decade mapping forgotten infrastructure across rural valleys before turning to horror. He writes about places that remember people better than people remember themselves.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Sorting his grandmother's estate, he reviews years of photographs and finds an old wooden chair appearing in every shot of her kitchen—closer in each image, though he never moved it. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the archivist realizes his archive has been editing itself, and something has been approaching him patiently for years.

chapters.title: Tunnels Not on Any Survey
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He maps tunnels beneath the village that contradict every official record, finding chalk marks and children's handprints leading to a dry well shaft. An old villager warns him away but hums a harvest song, stopping short of its last verse. The beat is compulsion: documentation becomes devotion as Dominic realizes the tunnels were dug toward him.

chapters.title: The Verse No One Sings
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, shifting briefly to the villager Maren's memories. On the night before the harvest moon, Maren confesses: the village promised a Thornbury child to the well generations ago, and the song's last verse is the words of acceptance every chosen child sang before descending. The beat is betrayal and grief—the found family he'd begun to trust built their lives on his sacrifice.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the well under the full moon, the chair waits at the shaft's edge and the song rises around him, pulling him toward the final verse. He sings every line but the last, then speaks his own ending—a refusal that collapses the tunnel and frees the previous chosen children's voices. The beat is hard-won belonging: the villagers stay with him in the wreckage, choosing him back.
